title: CDS Full Length Mock Test 07 (Hard Level)
description: Combined Defence Services Examination style full-length mock covering English, Elementary Mathematics and General Knowledge. Hard level, 100 questions.
instructions: There is a penalty of 0.83 marks for every wrong answer.
No marks will be deducted for unattempted questions.
Choose the most appropriate option among the four given choices.
The paper covers English, Elementary Mathematics and General Knowledge as in CDS.
Use of calculator or electronic device is not permitted.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the part that contains an error: Neither the battalion commander nor the company commanders / was informed / about the change / in the axis of advance.
options: Neither the battalion commander nor the company commanders
questions.explanation: When subjects joined by neither...nor differ in number, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Company commanders' is plural, so 'were informed' is required.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error: The brief, which were prepared / by the operations staff, / contained several / cartographic inaccuracies.
questions.explanation: 'Brief' is singular; the relative clause needs 'which was prepared'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error: Hardly the recce party had / returned to the RV / than the fog / closed in again.
questions.explanation: Correct form: 'Hardly had the recce party returned... when the fog...' (inversion + when, not than).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error: One of the sentries who / was posted on the ridge / have reported / unusual movement.
questions.explanation: The subject of the main clause is 'One', so the verb should be 'has reported'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the best improvement: The column will move at first light provided the weather holds.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is already correct: 'provided' + present simple for a future condition.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He insisted that the patrol is withdrawn before last light.
questions.explanation: After 'insisted that' the mandative subjunctive 'be withdrawn' is preferred in formal English.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: No sooner the bridge was blown than the enemy opened fire.
options: No sooner the bridge was blown
No sooner had the bridge been blown
No sooner the bridge had blown
questions.explanation: Correct inversion: 'No sooner had the bridge been blown than...'.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The general's order left the brigade with no ______ but to hold the pass.
questions.explanation: 'No alternative but to' is the fixed collocation.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The two accounts of the ambush are mutually ______.
questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive means they cannot both be true.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the synonym of INTRANSIGENT.
questions.explanation: Intransigent means unwilling to change one's views; uncompromising.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the synonym of PERFIDIOUS.
questions.explanation: Perfidy is betrayal of trust; perfidious = treacherous.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the antonym of SPURIOUS.
questions.explanation: Spurious means false or not genuine.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the antonym of TACITURN.
questions.explanation: Taciturn means reserved in speech; loquacious means talkative.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does 'to bite the bullet' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to face a difficult situation with courage.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: 'To steal a march on' someone means:
options: To gain an advantage by acting first
questions.explanation: It means to get ahead of a rival by acting before they do.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: 'A pyrrhic victory' is one that:
options: Costs so much it is almost a defeat
questions.explanation: Named after King Pyrrhus, whose victories against Rome were ruinously costly.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: 'To keep one's powder dry' means:
questions.explanation: Cromwell's advice: trust in God and keep your powder dry — stay prepared.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A person who is indifferent to pleasure and pain:
questions.explanation: A stoic cultivates indifference to fortune, pleasure and pain.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A statement open to more than one interpretation:
questions.explanation: Ambiguous statements admit two or more readings.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Change to passive: The sappers have laid the minefield along the defile.
options: The minefield has been laid along the defile by the sappers.
The minefield was laid by sappers.
The defile has laid the minefield.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active → present perfect passive with agent retained.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He said, "The convoy will reach the RV at 0400 hours."
options: He said that the convoy would reach the RV at 0400 hours.
He said that the convoy will reach.
questions.explanation: Will changes to would in reported speech after a past reporting verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Arrange: (P) across the river (Q) the engineers threw (R) under covering fire (S) a pontoon bridge
questions.explanation: 'The engineers threw a pontoon bridge across the river under covering fire.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The battalion was deployed ______ the ridgeline ______ first light.
questions.explanation: Deployed along a feature; at first light is the standard time phrase.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: ______ Himalayas form a formidable barrier ______ the north of India.
questions.explanation: Mountain ranges take 'the'; 'to the north' indicates direction.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A 'defile' in military usage is:
options: A narrow pass that constrains movement
questions.explanation: A defile is a constricted route such as a gorge or pass.

questions.question: If n = 2^4 × 3^2 × 5, the number of even factors of n is:
questions.explanation: Total factors = 5×3×2=30. Odd factors use only 3^2×5 → 3×2=6. Even factors = 30−6=24.

questions.explanation: Product of numbers = HCF × LCM. Other = (12×372)/36 = 124.
